BiblicalUsage: Balak was the king of Moab who feared Israel camped on his border, and he sent for Balaam to curse them. He watched in fury as blessing after blessing came out of the prophet's mouth instead.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Balak's story is God's plain answer to fear-driven scheming: no hired curse can touch a people God has blessed, and the king who tried hardest to stop Israel ended up paying to hear her blessed.
